skill: Linear Inequalities in One or Two Variables
stem: Which value of \(x\) satisfies the inequality \(3x - 7 > 14\)?
explanation: Solving \(3x - 7 > 14\) gives \(3x > 21\), so \(x > 7\). Among the choices, only 8 is greater than 7. The value 7 fails because the inequality is strict (not \(\geq\)). The value 5 results from an arithmetic slip such as dividing 14 by 3 instead of 21. The value 3 produces \(3(3) - 7 = 2\), which is far less than 14.

skill: Linear Inequalities in One or Two Variables
stem: A delivery service charges a flat fee of \$11 plus \$4 per mile. A customer has at most \$47 to spend on delivery. Which inequality represents the number of miles \(m\) the customer can afford, and what is the maximum whole number of miles?
explanation: The total cost is \(4m + 11\), which must be at most 47, giving \(4m + 11 \leq 47\). Solving: \(4m \leq 36\), so \(m \leq 9\). The maximum whole number of miles is 9. The distractor stating 10 miles uses the correct inequality but incorrectly rounds up from the exact answer of 9. The distractor with \(4m - 11\) subtracts the flat fee instead of adding it, inflating the result to 14. The distractor with \(11m + 4\) reverses the per-mile rate and flat fee, yielding only 3 miles.

skill: Linear Inequalities in One or Two Variables
stem: A small business produces two products, X and Y. Each unit of X requires 5 hours of labor and each unit of Y requires 3 hours. The business has at most 67 hours of labor available per week. Additionally, the business must produce at least 4 units of Y per week to meet a contract obligation. If the business wants to maximize the number of units of X produced per week, what is the maximum number of units of X it can produce?
explanation: The constraints are \(5x + 3y \leq 67\) and \(y \geq 4\). To maximize \(x\), set \(y\) to its minimum value of 4. Then \(5x + 3(4) \leq 67\), so \(5x + 12 \leq 67\), giving \(5x \leq 55\) and \(x \leq 11\). The maximum is 11 units. The value 10 comes from a subtraction error such as computing \(67 - 12\) as 50 instead of 55. The value 13 ignores the minimum Y constraint entirely and computes \(\lfloor 67/5 \rfloor = 13\). The value 9 results from using \(y = 5\) instead of the minimum of 4, obtaining \(\lfloor 52/5 \rfloor = 10\), then subtracting one extra unit.

skill: Systems of Two Linear Equations in Two Variables
stem:
What is the value of \(x\) in the solution to the system of equations below?
\[2x + y = 19\]
\[x - y = 5\]
explanation: Adding the two equations eliminates \(y\): \((2x + y) + (x - y) = 19 + 5\), which simplifies to \(3x = 24\), so \(x = 8\). Substituting back into the second equation gives \(8 - y = 5\), so \(y = 3\). The solution \((8, 3)\) satisfies both original equations: \(2(8) + 3 = 19\) and \(8 - 3 = 5\).

skill: Systems of Two Linear Equations in Two Variables
stem: A theater sells adult tickets for \$13 each and student tickets for \$7 each. For a particular show, 83 tickets were sold for a total revenue of \$893. How many student tickets were sold?
explanation: Let \(a\) be the number of adult tickets and \(s\) the number of student tickets. The system is \(a + s = 83\) and \(13a + 7s = 893\). Substituting \(a = 83 - s\): \(13(83 - s) + 7s = 893\), which gives \(1079 - 13s + 7s = 893\), so \(-6s = -186\) and \(s = 31\). The value 52 is the number of adult tickets, not student tickets, resulting from answering the wrong quantity. The value 38 arises from setting up the revenue equation with swapped prices (using 7 for adults and 13 for students). The value 45 comes from an arithmetic error during the simplification step.

skill: Systems of Two Linear Equations in Two Variables
stem: A chemist has two acid solutions. Solution P is 23% acid and Solution Q is 61% acid. The chemist needs to mix the two solutions to produce exactly 19 liters of a 37% acid solution. How many liters of Solution Q are needed?
explanation: Let \(p\) be the liters of Solution P and \(q\) be the liters of Solution Q. The system is \(p + q = 19\) and \(0.23p + 0.61q = 0.37(19) = 7.03\). Substituting \(p = 19 - q\): \(0.23(19 - q) + 0.61q = 7.03\), giving \(4.37 - 0.23q + 0.61q = 7.03\), so \(0.38q = 2.66\) and \(q = 7\). The value 12 is the number of liters of Solution P, not Solution Q, resulting from misreading which quantity the question asks for. The value 9 arises from incorrectly setting up the acid concentration equation, such as using 37 instead of 0.37. The value 5 results from an arithmetic error when dividing 2.66 by 0.38.
